# Discover site URLs with `web_map`

`web_map` gives an agent URLs discovered from a website's page links and sitemaps.

## When to use it

Use it when the agent knows the website but needs to find relevant pages, such as a company's pricing page or a documentation section. Pair it with [`web_fetch`](web_fetch.html) so the agent can choose which URLs to read.

Choose [`web_search`](web_search.html) to find sources across the web, or [`web_crawl`](web_crawl.html) to follow links and read multiple pages in one call.

## Quick example

```python
from serpapi_search_tools import web_fetch, web_map

agent_tools = [web_map(), web_fetch()]
```

With one supported SDK installed, these tools are native to that SDK. Add them to your agent's tool collection. See [Agent SDKs](frameworks.html) for setup and explicit provider selection when multiple SDKs are installed.

An agent can start discovery with:

```json
{"url": "https://www.python.org/about/"}
```

## Inputs the agent can provide

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `url` | string | yes | The absolute HTTP or HTTPS URL to start discovering links from |

The agent supplies only `url`. The tool fixes the Extract API operation to `map`; sitemap and subdomain settings stay in application code.

## Configure the tool

| Constructor option | Default | Use it for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `provider` | `"auto"` | Detect one installed SDK or select an SDK explicitly |
| `default_params` | `None` | Control sitemap and subdomain discovery |
| `mode` | `compact` | Select URL fields for JSON output; use `"full"` to retain all JSON fields |
| `response_format` | `markdown` | Return the API's Markdown link list, or choose `"json"` for structured fields |
| `timeout` | `None` | Set the SDK request timeout in seconds |
| `name` | `"web_map"` | Give a configured discovery tool a distinct name |

The tool also accepts `api_key`, `client`, and `include_examples`. See [Common configuration](configuration.html) for authentication and shared options.

## Useful SerpApi parameters

Set discovery options in `default_params`:

| Parameter | API default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `include_sitemap` | `True` | Also discover URLs from the website's sitemaps |
| `include_subdomains` | `False` | Include other subdomains of the same website; otherwise keep links on the same host |

For an agent that should choose from links on the supplied page, turn off sitemap discovery:

```python
from serpapi_search_tools import web_fetch, web_map

linked_pages = web_map(
    default_params={"include_sitemap": False},
    name="linked_pages",
)
agent_tools = [linked_pages, web_fetch()]
```

Set `include_subdomains=True` when relevant pages also live on hosts such as `docs.example.com` or `blog.example.com`.

## What comes back

By default, the tool returns the API's Markdown list of links unchanged. Map results help the agent select pages; use `web_fetch` to read their content.

| Configuration | Returned value |
| --- | --- |
| Default, or any Markdown configuration | The API's Markdown link list unchanged |
| `response_format="json"` | A JSON string with a `urls` list containing `url`, `title`, and `source` when present |
| `mode="full", response_format="json"` | The complete JSON response, including metadata |

A successful compact JSON map with no links returns `{"urls":[]}`. If a Google or Bing search URL redirects to its dedicated engine, Markdown preserves that engine's response. Use full JSON to read a redirected engine's structured results; compact JSON raises when the expected `urls` list is unavailable.

## Common mistakes

- Expecting page content in map results. Give the agent `web_fetch` as well when it needs to read a page.
- Assuming every discovered URL has a title. Link fields depend on the source.
- Leaving sitemap discovery enabled when only links from the supplied page are needed.
- Passing `max_pages` or `max_depth` to control discovery. Those settings belong to `web_crawl`.
